body:
## Summary

On a Google Pixel 11 Pro (Imagination PowerVR C-Series CXTP-48-1536 MC1, `VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY`, Vulkan 1.4.317, `subgroupSize=128`, `maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations=1024`, `maxComputeSharedMemorySize=32768`), the Vulkan backend crashes the GPU firmware during prompt processing.

Every compute pipeline compiles. The first 128-token batch returns from `llama_decode`. About 9 seconds after the context is created, Android logs a PowerVR subsystem restart, the compositor wedges, and the device usually reboots. No tokens are produced.

The same app and models work on a Pixel 8 Pro (ARM Mali/Immortalis).

I don't expect a fix in llama.cpp; the fault is almost certainly in Imagination's driver. This is filed so the next person who tries Vulkan on a Tensor G6 finds it, and in case the subgroup-128 detail suggests a workaround to someone who knows the backend.

## Android's GPU crash record

`adb shell dumpsys dropbox --print | grep -A12 SubsystemRestart` gives a per-crash reason. Across builds:

| llama.cpp | flash attn | submissions | OS build | crash reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| b10621 | on | default | 2026-07 | `GUILTY_OVERRUNING` |
| b10731 | on | default | 2026-07 | `[0]:[addr=0x8056288700]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]` |
| b10731 | off | default | 2026-07 | `[0]:[addr=0x805730fd80]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]` |
| b10731 | on | serialised | 2026-07 and 2026-09 | `GUILTY_OVERRUNING` |
| b10731 | on | default | 2026-09 | `[0]:[addr=0x8047852d80]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]` |

`GUILTY_OVERRUNING` reads as a job that never terminated and hit the GPU watchdog. `FW_PAGEFAULT` reads as an MMU fault on an unmapped GPU address. The fault address is stable within a process (allocations move between runs), so the access is deterministic rather than a race.

`b10621 -> b10731` changed the failure class but fixed nothing.

## Ruled out, all measured on the device

- llama.cpp version: b10621 and b10731 (the latter includes #27726's warptile clamp for subgroup > 64).
- Flash attention: `LLAMA_FLASH_ATTN_TYPE_DISABLED` for this vendor. No change.
- Submission structure: `GGML_VK_SERIALIZE_SUBMISSIONS=1`. No change except the crash class. Since every submit then waits for completion, this also shows that the first 128-token chunk finishes on the GPU and a later one faults. It is not a cross-submission race.
- Memory: reproduced on a fresh boot with 14 GB available and zero swap.
- Model architecture: a hybrid model (Qwen 3.5 2B, gated delta net + SSM) and a plain transformer (Gemma 4 E2B) fail identically.
- Quantisation: `Q4_0` crashes exactly like `Q4_K_M` and `UD-Q4_K_XL`. This matters because a user on Imagination's own forum found that on the Pixel 10's D-series DXT-48-1536, k-quant compute shaders return wrong results while `Q4_0`, `Q5_0`, `Q8_0`, `F16` and `F32` are correct (https://forums.imgtec.com/t/powervr-dxt-48-1536-incorrect-results-from-k-quant-vulkan-compute-shaders-in-llama-cpp/4291). That is a different bug. The D-series computes wrong answers; the C-series crashes its firmware.
- Driver: the September 2026 Pixel OTA (`CD1A.260905.001.A1`, new vendor image) behaves identically. The driver still reports 1.4.317.

## Configuration

Vulkan only, all layers offloaded, `n_batch=128`, `n_ctx=7168-7424`, prompt of about 2,850 to 3,000 tokens, `type_k` and `type_v` left at F16.

## Related

- #8437: Vulkan on an Imagination GPU (RISC-V, warp size 1). Different symptom, stale.
- #25734: Adreno `subgroupSize=128`, wrong matmul results, fixed by #27726.
- pytorch/executorch#17299: PowerVR D-series on the Pixel 10 Pro produced all-zero outputs from ExecuTorch's Vulkan backend, root-caused to a command-sequencing defect where dispatches after the first in a command buffer lost their writes.

## Repro

So far only reproduced from an app embedding libllama, not from `llama-bench`. I can run a standalone repro on the device if someone suggests the exact invocation. Each attempt costs a reboot.

comments.body:
Great writeup. subgroupSize=128 on PowerVR’s driver is likely triggering a driver SPIR-V compiler bug during subgroup shuffles/broadcasts in ggml-vulkan.cpp, leading to the firmware pagefaults and watchdog hangs.

To run a standalone repro via ADB without your app wrapper:

***adb push llama-bench /data/local/tmp/
adb push model.gguf /data/local/tmp/
adb shell "chmod +x /data/local/tmp/llama-bench && /data/local/tmp/llama-bench -m /data/local/tmp/model.gguf -p 1024 -n 0 -ngl 99"***


A couple quick things to test:

GGML_VK_DISABLE_F16=1 (rules out PowerVR FP16 ALU driver bugs)
If you temporarily disable subgroup ops or hardcode subgroup size in ggml-vulkan.cpp, does prompt processing succeed? If that fixes it, we could add a driver vendor check for VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY to bypass subgroup matmul paths on C-series hardware.

I built `test-backend-ops` and `llama-bench` for Android arm64 and ran them on the device. There turned out to be several separate problems rather than one, so this is a correction to my original report as much as an update.

@ZitouniNidhal you were right that it is a driver shader compiler bug, though not in the way either of us expected.

### 1. Dequant mul_mat_vec pipelines fail to compile (fixed, PR linked below)

`vkCreateComputePipelines` returns `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN` for every dequant `mul_mat_vec` shader built with the subgroup-only reduction: Q2_K through Q6_K, TQ2_0, the IQ types, MXFP4, NVFP4. ggml rethrows and the process aborts on the first generated token. Legacy quants compile fine.

Not the subgroup width: 32, 64 and 128 all fail, as does dropping the full-subgroups flag and the required-subgroup-size pNext. Shared-memory reduction compiles and is correct. PR: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28341

This one aborts cleanly. It is not what crashes the GPU firmware.

### 2. FLASH_ATTN_EXT is wrong, and can hang the GPU

`test-backend-ops -o FLASH_ATTN_EXT` by head size:

| hsk | passed | failed |
|---|---|---|
| 40 | 0 | 226 |
| 64 | 2038 | 0 |
| 72 | 745 | 102 |
| 80 | 92 | 22 |
| 256 | passes at kv=1024/nb=32; fails at kv=1024/nb=64 and at kv=2048 | |

Failures are `ERR ≈ 1.0`, so the output is unrelated to the reference rather than slightly off.

The head-size-72 run also wedged the GPU. `dumpsys dropbox` recorded `powervr - [988]:[surfaceflinger]:[GUILTY_OVERRUNING]`, the compositor froze, and the test process hung until its timeout. Head sizes 96 and 256 were only partly covered because I stopped the sweep after that.

### 3. FW_PAGEFAULT at large context (still open, and this is the one from the original report)

With the pipeline fix applied and flash attention disabled, inference at `n_ctx=7168` still kills the firmware:

```
crash reason: powervr - [0]:[addr=0x80652c9f80]:[FW_PAGEFAULT]
```

`llama-bench -p 128` runs clean end to end. `-p 7168` page-faults. `GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=8` does not prevent it, so it is not submission length. An unmapped GPU read rather than a watchdog kill, so it is a different failure from #2. I have not isolated it further yet.

### 4. Results are not reproducible run to run

Same binary, same input, three consecutive runs of `test-backend-ops -o GET_ROWS`: 102, 99, 100 of 115 passing. `MUL_MAT -p type_a=iq2_xxs`: 14 then 15 of 27. All failures are IQ types.

The k-quants are stable by contrast, 26/26 on Q4_K across four runs, so this is not general flakiness in the harness.

Filed separately as #28343.

### 5. Unrelated, small

`mul_mat_vec_bf16_f32_f32` is created unconditionally at `ggml-vulkan.cpp:5374` regardless of whether the device supports bf16. This device reports `bf16: 0` and its compiler rejects that shader, so anything requesting a bf16 mul_mat_vec aborts. Filed as #28342.

### Reproducing

```
cmake -S . -B build-android -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$NDK/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake \
  -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-31 \
  -DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=ON
adb push build-android/bin/test-backend-ops /data/local/tmp/
adb shell /data/local/tmp/test-backend-ops test -b Vulkan0 -o MUL_MAT -p type_a=q4_K,
```

`adb shell dumpsys dropbox --print | grep -A12 SubsystemRestart` is what gives the firmware crash reason.

I would suggest keeping this issue for #3, since that is the firmware crash the title describes and the only one still unexplained.

This now looks like a separate address/memory-range problem rather than a submission or watchdog issue.

Since:

- -p 128 completes cleanly
- -p 7168 reproducibly triggers FW_PAGEFAULT
- FLASH_ATTN_EXT is disabled
- GGML_VK_MAX_NODES_PER_SUBMIT=8 does not change the result

I would focus on isolating the first context length where the fault appears and determining which Vulkan operation introduces the invalid GPU read.

A useful next step would be a binary search over prompt/context length (e.g. 1024, 2048, 4096, 5120, 6144, 7168) with the same model and binary. If there is a stable threshold, that strongly suggests a size-dependent buffer/offset/addressing issue rather than a random kernel failure.

I would then instrument the Vulkan backend to log the tensor/buffer ranges and the operation immediately before each submission around the failing threshold. In particular, check for offsets or buffer ranges that exceed the allocated VkBuffer size once the KV/context tensors grow.

If the same operation can be reproduced in test-backend-ops with dimensions matching the failing sequence length, that would give us a minimal driver repro.

For a permanent llama.cpp workaround, if this is confirmed to be a PowerVR address-range issue, I would prefer a vendor-specific safe path (chunking the affected operation or splitting the large buffer access) for VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY, rather than globally reducing context size.

That should preserve correctness and avoid the firmware crash while keeping the normal path unchanged for other drivers.

Update with new measurements. The context-length lead is dead, and there is a worse problem underneath it.

@ZitouniNidhal on your suggestions:

GGML_VK_DISABLE_F16=1 does not help. Still garbage output.

The vendor check for VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY is already up as #28341. It fixes the pipeline compile failure. It does not make this device produce correct results.

On the binary search over context length: I ran it, and there is no threshold. Standalone llama-bench at my app's settings (-b 128 -ub 128 -fa off) completes cleanly at p=2048, p=4096 and p=7168, and generates cleanly at depth 7168. My earlier "p=7168 page-faults" was llama-bench's default batching (-b 2048 -ub 512), which is a much larger graph, so that was my mistake. The app then crashed at n_ctx=6656, which is smaller than the standalone run that survives. Context size is not the trigger.

The part that matters more: this device computes wrong numbers without crashing.

llama-completion, standalone, `-ngl 99 -c 6656 -b 128 -ub 128 -fa off --temp 0 --seed 1`, prompt "The capital of France is Paris. The capital of Japan is Tokyo. Write three sentences about why the sky appears blue.":

```
stra。。肠肠肠爱ippo
   >>>是是
 2016 年 1 月 1 日，在 1999 年 1 月 1 日，在 1999 年 1 月 1 日
```

The GPU fault counter was identical before and after. No firmware fault, no hang. The device just returns junk.

The output is also different every time. 14 runs across 7 configurations, all greedy with a fixed seed, same binary, model and prompt:

baseline, `GGML_VK_DISABLE_F16`, `GGML_VK_DISABLE_FUSION`, `GGML_VK_DISABLE_MMVQ`, `GGML_VK_DISABLE_ASYNC`, shared-memory dmmv reduction, hybrid dmmv reduction.

Every one produced garbage, and no two runs matched. Greedy decoding should be byte-identical run to run, so this looks like a race or uninitialized memory rather than a wrong kernel. The hybrid reduction failing the same way also rules out #28341 as the cause.

I could not get a CPU-side comparison on this phone. CPU-only runs time out before emitting a token, so I have no `-ngl 0` baseline to show you.

One thing from outside llama.cpp that may be relevant. Chrome's Dawn force-disables `VulkanUseZeroInitializeWorkgroupMemoryExtension` for all Imagination devices, with the comment "Pixel 10 workgroup zero init does not always work as expected" (crbug.com/479242793). Dawn also enables `VulkanPolyfilSwitchWithIf` for this driver ("polyfill for case switch with large ranges"), enables `VulkanIncompletePipelineCacheWorkaround` on Pixel 10, and denies maximal reconvergence on `IsAndroidImgTec()`. Workgroup memory that is not reliably zeroed would fit non-deterministic compute results.

test-backend-ops does not catch any of this. `run_whole_graph()` defaults to false and the comparator runs the graph one node at a time, so every individual op I tested passes, including all k-quant MUL_MAT and the hybrid and recurrent ops, while the assembled model produces garbage. What does catch it in about ten seconds is a greedy canary: `--temp 0 -n 16` on a short prompt, and check that the output is coherent English.

I am not asking anyone to fix this driver. I have disabled the vendor in my own app. I am reporting it in case you would rather llama.cpp refuse `VK_DRIVER_ID_IMAGINATION_PROPRIETARY`, or at least warn on it, than emit silently wrong tokens, which is what it does today. Chrome, PlayCanvas and Construct 3 have all ended up blocking this vendor for WebGPU for related reasons.

title: Vulkan: GPU firmware crashes on Imagination PowerVR C-series (Pixel 11 Pro, Tensor G6, subgroupSize 128)
